questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL 18 query uses `last_value(value) OVER (ORDER BY ts)` with unique timestamps. Why can it return the current row instead of the partition final value?

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Window Functions
sources.claim: The default ordered frame ends at the current row peer group. With unique timestamps that is the current row. last_value reads the frame, not automatically the whole partition; it does not ignore ordering or restrict to NULL rows.

questions.explanation: The default ordered frame ends at the current row peer group. With unique timestamps that is the current row. last_value reads the frame, not automatically the whole partition; it does not ignore ordering or restrict to NULL rows.

choices.text: last_value always ignores ORDER BY and returns an arbitrary partition value.
The default frame always contains only rows with NULL ordering values.
Every window function automatically rewrites its frame to the full partition.
The default frame ends at the current row last peer.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL 18 FROM subquery needs columns from an earlier FROM item. Which keyword permits that correlation?

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Table Expressions
sources.claim: LATERAL enables references to preceding FROM items. DISTINCT changes duplicate handling, ORDER BY changes order, and UNION combines results rather than granting this correlation scope.

questions.explanation: LATERAL enables references to preceding FROM items. DISTINCT changes duplicate handling, ORDER BY changes order, and UNION combines results rather than granting this correlation scope.

choices.text: `LATERAL` on the referencing subquery.
`DISTINCT` on the referencing subquery to enable cross-item scope.
`ORDER BY` on the earlier item to export its columns into every subquery.
`UNION` on the referencing subquery to copy the previous item bindings.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL 18 recursive CTE walks a graph that can contain cycles. Which termination statements are correct? Select all that apply.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: WITH Queries (Common Table Expressions)
sources.claim: A and B distinguish set and bag behavior. D handles cycles that whole-row deduplication misses. C is false because changing depth makes rows distinct; E is false because termination depends on the query, not a universal iteration cap.

questions.explanation: A and B distinguish set and bag behavior. D handles cycles that whole-row deduplication misses. C is false because changing depth makes rows distinct; E is false because termination depends on the query, not a universal iteration cap.

choices.text: UNION removes duplicate result rows during recursive evaluation.
UNION ALL by itself does not eliminate revisited rows.
Adding a changing depth column guarantees UNION detects every graph cycle.
Track visited keys or use CYCLE when duplicate whole-row detection is insufficient.
Every recursive CTE stops after a fixed automatic iteration count.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL 18 last_value calculation should see the last row of the entire ordered partition. Which frame expresses that requirement?

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Window Functions
sources.claim: Unbounded following extends the frame to the partition end. Current-row endpoints exclude later rows, and a one-row lookback cannot include the full partition.

questions.explanation: Unbounded following extends the frame to the partition end. Current-row endpoints exclude later rows, and a one-row lookback cannot include the full partition.

choices.text: `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`.
`ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW` for the entire ordered partition.
`ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` for every later row.
`ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` to include all future partition rows.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL 18 LATERAL subquery can return zero rows for a parent. Which join preserves that parent in the result?

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Table Expressions
sources.claim: LEFT JOIN preserves an unmatched left row with NULL right columns. Cross and inner joins do not create a right-side row when the subquery is empty; false inner-join conditions remove matches.

questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves an unmatched left row with NULL right columns. Cross and inner joins do not create a right-side row when the subquery is empty; false inner-join conditions remove matches.

choices.text: `CROSS JOIN LATERAL (...)` because cross joins keep unmatched parents.
`LEFT JOIN LATERAL (...) ON true`.
`INNER JOIN LATERAL (...) ON true` because true creates missing rows.
`JOIN LATERAL (...) ON false` because false preserves the outer row.

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL 18 recursive graph query emits both node id and increasing depth. Which cycle-handling claims hold? Select all that apply.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: WITH Queries (Common Table Expressions)
sources.claim: A: duplicate elimination compares complete output rows. B and D provide cycle-aware handling. C falsely ignores depth. E is false because joins or sorts can force complete recursive evaluation; outer LIMIT is not a universal safety strategy.

questions.explanation: A: duplicate elimination compares complete output rows. B and D provide cycle-aware handling. C falsely ignores depth. E is false because joins or sorts can force complete recursive evaluation; outer LIMIT is not a universal safety strategy.

choices.text: A repeated node with a new depth can remain a distinct UNION row.
A visited-node path can prevent recursion through a previously visited node.
UNION deduplicates solely by node id even when depth is another output column.
The CYCLE clause can mark cycles and help stop the recursive walk.
LIMIT outside the CTE guarantees safe termination for every joined and sorted query.
